question.leadin: This country's emperor, Menelik II, stopped an Italian invasion of his country at the Battle of Adwa.
question.text: Along with Liberia, what nation in the Horn of Africa led from Addis Ababa is considered to be the only African nation not to be colonized?
question.clue: Under a communist regime called "The Derg" in the 1980s, many died in a famine worsened by harsh policies against this country's Tigray people.

swap.leadin: Identify the African country based on the event from the 1990s.
swap.text: In 1991, this West African country moved its capital from Lagos to Abuja.
swap.clue: The exploitation of this country's Ogoni people by Royal Dutch Shell was opposed by activist Ken Saro-Wiwa, who was executed by this country's dictator Sani Abacha.

question.text: Gaddafi led this North African country, which disputed the Aouzou Strip with its southern neighbor, Chad. The U.S. embassy in this country's city of Benghazi was attacked in 2012.
question.clue: The arch of Septimius Severus is located in its Roman ruins of Leptis Magna, while the Jabal Akhdar or "Green Mountain" rises to the east of this nation's second-largest city, Benghazi.

swap.leadin: Jomo Kenyatta was a leader of the militant group that headed this movement.
swap.text: Name this violent 1950s movement, a rebellion of the Kikuyu people against their European colonizers.
swap.clue: Evelyn Baring declared a state of emergency in response to this revolt and helped oversee Operation Anvil, which forcibly relocated people from Nairobi.

question.text: At the Battle of Tondibi, the Moroccan army defeated the forces of Askia Ishaq II, who in 1588 took power in this African empire, a center of Trans-Saharan trade.
question.clue: Forces of this empire were lead by Ishaq II when it lost to Moroccan forces at Tondibi.

swap.text: This socialist party in Algeria sought independence from France, and they were the perpetrators of the Oran massacre of 1962.
swap.clue: This group was at the front of the drive for Algerian independence. It eliminated the rival MNA faction in the Cafe Wars.

question.text: The Granadan architect al-Sahili designed this mosque and university for Mansa Musa. Along with the Djinguereber and Sidi Yahia, this institution comprised a center of higher learning in Timbuktu.
question.answerHtml: Sankore University (or Sankore Madrasah; or Sankore Mosque; or Sankore Masjid)
question.clue: This institution constructed by the Granadan architect al-Sahili, which was home to the Fula scholar Modibo Mohammed Al Kaburi.

swap.leadin: This event forced Cecil Rhodes to resign as governor of the Cape Colony, after he was led to believe it would not happen.
swap.text: Name this event, which occurred when the namesake British statesman attacked the Traansvaal Republic in late December 1895.
swap.clue: Although this event was ultimately a failure, as it intended to trigger an uprising among the Uitlanders ] in Transvaal, it was a major cause of the Second Boer War.

question.leadin: According to an oft-repeated story, Robert Baden-Powell based the scouting salute on a gesture made by this empire's ruler Prempeh.
question.text: Name this empire with its capital at Kumasi. The final war between Britain and this empire began with Frederick Mitchell Hodgson's demand to sit on the Golden Stool.
question.clue: That king was aided by Okomfo Anokye, who set up the obirempon as local magistrates and codified this empire's laws after it gained independence from the Denkyera.

swap.leadin: Name these African leaders under fire.
swap.text: Protests continued through 2003 against this dictator of Zimbabwe.
swap.clue: This leader's G-40-backed wife and a military-backed member of the ZANU both vied to succeed him as president after a 2017 coup.

question.text: Soweto and other apartheid-era atrocities were investigated by the Truth and Reconciliation Commission set up in the 1990s by this first black president of South Africa.
question.clue: According to Heather Ann Thompson's book Blood in the Water, this man led an extensive cover-up of his disastrous mismanagement after deploying 600 national guard members in the middle of September 1971 hostage negotiations.

swap.leadin: The Fawcett Commission investigated conditions in concentration camps during this war.
swap.text: Name this war fought between the British and the namesake Afrikaans-speaking group, who fought to maintain the independence of the Transvaal Republic and the Orange Free State.
swap.answerHtml: Second Anglo-Boer War [do not accept or prompt on the First Boer War]
swap.clue: Emily Hobhouse founded a Distress Fund for victims of this war, and concentration camps set up during it were investigated by Millicent Fawcett.

question.leadin: Gordon Sprigg's implementation of the 1878 Peace Preservation Act resulted in the natives of this country rebelling in the 1880 Gun War.
question.text: Name this modern-day country where Moorosi and his sons were beheaded and skinned after he led a failed uprising of Basuto tribespeople against annexation by the Cape Colony.
question.clue: An 1880s Gun War in this modern-day country was led by Lerotholi and Masopha.

swap.text: This president of the Movement for the Survival of the Ogoni People campaigned against Royal Dutch Shell's destruction of Ogoni lands. He was hanged on the orders of Sani Abacha's government.
swap.clue: This man wrote the memoir A Month and a Day recounting his detention by the government of Ibrahim Babangida.

question.leadin: According to legend, this island was sold to an exiled Persian prince by a Bantu king for "as much colored cloth as could cover its circumference."
question.text: Name this island, which became an important port in Indian ocean trade and lends its name to a sultanate that ruled over the Swahili coast.
question.clue: Battuta's most southerly destination was this city in modern Tanzania, where he described its Great Mosque made from coral. This city's namesake sultanate dominated the Swahili coast in the fifteenth century.

swap.leadin: Zuma Rock is known as the "Gateway to" this city, which lies inside the Federal Capital Territory.
swap.text: Name this planned city that became its nation's capital in 1991.

question.text: This mercenary of Irish blood was hired by Moise Tshombe to put down the Simba rebellion in the Congo. In 1981, he and his drinking buddies in Ye Ancient Order of Froth Blowers created a fake rugby team that tried to overthrow the president of the Seychelles; that plan failed.
question.answerHtml: Mike Hoare [or Thomas Michael Hoare; or Mad Mike Hoare]

swap.leadin: This state was established by Muhammad Abdullah Hassan, known to the British as the Mad Mullah, who organized its army into seven regiments.
swap.text: Name this revolutionary Sunni state in the Horn of Africa from 1896 to 1920, which fought against European powers during the Scramble for Africa.
swap.answerHtml: Dervish State [or Dawlada Daraawiish; or Dawlat ad-Darawish; prompt on “Somaliland” or “Somalia”; do NOT accept “British Somaliland”]

question.leadin: After emerging from the poolside bathroom where he was hiding, this leader recited the first surah of the Quran to pacify the soldiers trying to overthrow him during his 42nd birthday party.
question.text: Name this member of the 'Alawi dynasty, who convinced treasonous pilots to stop shooting his plane by radioing, "The tyrant is dead!" This king, who used the secret Tazmamart prison during his country's Years of Lead, also authorized the Green March to expel Spain from Western Sahara.
question.answerHtml: Hassan II [accept Mawlay al-Hassan bin Mohammed bin Yusef al-Alawi; prompt on just Hassan]

swap.text: Subtitled "First Steps for Uganda to Move to the Left," this 1969 document written by Obote outlined his plan for wealth redistribution.
